questions.stem: Read: 「ゆきさん、お元気ですか。先週、家族と京都に行きました。お寺がたくさんあって、とてもきれいでした。ゆきさんにおみやげを買いましたよ。来月会えるのを楽しみにしています。ケイトより」 What type of text is this?
options: A personal message to a friend
An advertisement for a tour of Kyoto
A formal letter to a teacher
A diary entry written for herself
questions.explanation: It is addressed to ゆきさん, shares news, and is signed 「ケイトより」, 'from Kate'. A diary is not addressed to anyone, and nothing in it sells a tour.

questions.stem: Read the email: 「山田先生、すみませんが、かぜをひいてしまったので、明日のじゅぎょうを休みます。しゅくだいは金曜日に出してもいいでしょうか。トム」 What does Tom ask?
options: Whether the teacher is feeling better now
Whether he can do a different homework task
Whether he may hand in homework on Friday
Whether tomorrow's class has been cancelled
questions.explanation: 「〜てもいいでしょうか」 asks politely for permission: 'may I hand it in on Friday?'. The cold is Tom's, which is why he will miss the class.

questions.stem: In the email 「山田先生、すみませんが、明日のじゅぎょうを休みます。」, which features show it is written to a teacher?
options: Plain forms and endings such as 「よ」 and 「ね」
A comment on the season before any news
The reader's name followed by 「より」
「先生」 after the name and polite です/ます forms
questions.explanation: 「先生」 is the title for a teacher, and 「すみませんが」 and 「休みます」 are polite. Plain forms with 「よ」 and 「ね」 would suit a friend, and 「より」 goes after the writer's name, not the reader's.

questions.stem: Read the message: 「メールありがとう。土曜日は午前中アルバイトがあるから、午後二時ごろなら会えるよ。駅の前で待ってるね。」 When and where will they meet?
options: At exactly 2 pm, inside the station
At about 2 pm, in front of the station
In the morning, in front of the station
At about 2 pm, at the writer's workplace
questions.explanation: 「午前中アルバイトがあるから」 rules out the morning, and 「午後二時ごろなら」 is 'if it's around 2 pm'. 「駅の前」 is in front of the station, and 「ごろ」 means 'about', not exactly.

questions.stem: In the message 「土曜日は午後二時ごろなら会えるよ。駅の前で待ってるね。」, what shows the writer is writing to a friend?
options: A title such as 「さま」 after the reader's name
Plain forms with endings such as 「よ」 and 「ね」
The polite request form 「〜てください」
A seasonal greeting before the main news
questions.explanation: 「会える」 and 「待ってる」 are plain forms, and 「よ」 and 「ね」 make the tone chatty. A message to a teacher would say 「会えます」 and 「待っています」.

questions.stem: Read: 「ホームステイの間、いろいろおせわになりました。毎日、日本の家族と晩ご飯を食べたり、話したりして、とても楽しかったです。オーストラリアにも、ぜひ来てください。」 Who is writing, and to whom?
options: A student about to leave, to a teacher
A host family, to a student who will arrive soon
A student who has gone home, to the host family
The host family, to the student's own parents
questions.explanation: 「おせわになりました」 thanks people who looked after you, 「日本の家族」 is how a guest refers to a host family, and the invitation to Australia shows the writer lives there.

questions.stem: Read the message: 「来週の土曜日、私のたんじょう日パーティーをします。昼十二時から私の家で。来られるかどうか、木曜日までに教えてね。」 What does the writer want?
options: Everyone to arrive at the party before twelve
To know by Thursday if the reader can come
Someone to bring food to the party on Saturday
The reader to come to her house on Thursday
questions.explanation: 「来られるかどうか」 is 'whether or not you can come', and 「木曜日までに教えて」 is 'tell me by Thursday'. The party itself is on Saturday at twelve.

questions.stem: A formal email to a company ends 「おへんじをお待ちしております。」 What does the writer mean?
options: I have waited a long time for your reply.
I look forward to your reply.
I am replying to your email.
Please wait for my reply.
questions.explanation: 「お待ちしております」 is the humble, very polite form of 「待っています」, 'I am waiting', so it is a courteous way to close. It does not complain about a delay; that would need words like 「まだ」.

questions.stem: A library notice says 「としょかんの中では、食べたり飲んだりしてはいけません。」 What does it mean?
options: Food and drink are sold in the library
Eat and drink before you enter the library
You must not eat or drink in the library
You may eat but not drink in the library
questions.explanation: 「〜たり〜たり」 lists examples of actions, eating and drinking, and 「〜てはいけません」 forbids them. It covers both, not just one.

questions.stem: A shop sign says 「本日は午後五時で終わります。」 What does it tell customers?
options: The shop opens at 5 pm today
The shop is closed all day today
The sale ends at 5 pm tomorrow
The shop closes at 5 pm today
questions.explanation: 「本日」 (ほんじつ) is a formal word for 'today', and 「五時で終わります」 is 'finishes at five'. Opening would be 「あきます」 or 「始まります」.

questions.stem: Read the notice: 「プールは毎週月曜日がお休みです。ただし、八月十三日から十六日までは、月曜日もあいています。」 When is the pool closed?
options: On Mondays and from 13 to 16 August
Only from 13 to 16 August
On Mondays, except from 13 to 16 August
Every day from 13 to 16 August
questions.explanation: 「月曜日がお休み」 is the rule, and 「ただし」, 'however', introduces the exception: from the 13th to the 16th it is open on Mondays too. The dates are extra opening, not extra closing.

questions.stem: Read the notice: 「九月十日の土曜日に、学校でぶんかさいがあります。午前十時から午後三時までです。どなたでも来ることができます。」 Who may come?
options: Anyone at all
Only students' families
Only students at the school
Only people who have booked
questions.explanation: 「どなたでも」 is the polite form of 「だれでも」, 'anyone', and 「来ることができます」 is 'can come'. Nothing limits it to families or students.

questions.stem: A homestay house rule says 「おふろに入る前に、体を洗ってください。おふろのおゆは、ぬかないでください。」 What are guests asked to do?
options: Wash in the bath, then let the water out afterwards
Take a bath first, then wash your hair afterwards
Let the water out of the bath once you have finished
Wash first, and leave the water in the bath
questions.explanation: 「入る前に」 is 'before getting in', and 「ぬかないで」 is 'please don't let it out'. In Japan you wash outside the tub, and the family shares the same hot water.

questions.stem: Read the school notice: 「来週の月曜日は、エアコンのこうじのため、じゅぎょうは午前中だけです。」 Why are classes only in the morning?
options: Because Monday is a public holiday
Because the weather will be very hot
Because of work on the air conditioning
Because of a meeting for teachers
questions.explanation: Noun + 「のため」 can give a reason, 'because of', and 「こうじ」 is building or repair work. 「午前中だけ」 is 'only in the morning'.

questions.stem: Read the postcard: 「今、北海道に来ています。雪がたくさんふって、毎日スキーをしています。」 What is the writer doing?
options: Swimming at the beach in Hokkaidō
Waiting for snow to fall in Hokkaidō
Skiing every day in Hokkaidō
Planning a ski trip to Hokkaidō
questions.explanation: 「来ています」 means she is there now, and 「毎日スキーをしています」 is 'I'm skiing every day'. 「雪がたくさんふって」 shows there is plenty of snow already.

questions.stem: Read the blog: 「先週の日曜日、友だちと山にのぼりました。朝は雨がふっていましたが、昼ごろにははれて、上から見たけしきはさいこうでした。」 What was the weather like?
options: Rain in the morning, clear by midday
Clear in the morning, rainy by midday
Rainy all day, so they turned back early
Clear all day, with a great view
questions.explanation: 「朝は雨がふっていました」 is 'it was raining in the morning', and 「が、昼ごろにははれて」 turns to 'but around noon it cleared'. The great view came after the rain stopped.

questions.stem: Read the blog: 「一日スマホを使わない生活をしてみました。はじめは何をしたらいいか分からなかったけれど、夜には本を一さつ読み終わっていました。思っていたより楽しかったです。」 How did it go?
options: Better than she expected
As dull as she expected
She gave up before the evening
She read on her phone all evening
questions.explanation: 「はじめは…分からなかったけれど」 admits a slow start, and 「思っていたより楽しかった」 is 'more fun than I'd thought'. Finishing a whole book shows how well she filled the time.

questions.stem: Read: 「日本の夏はむしあついです。とくに東京は、夜になってもあまりすずしくなりません。」 What is the general point, rather than a specific detail?
options: Nights in Japan are cool in summer
Summer in Japan is hot and humid
Tokyo stays warm even at night
Summer in Tokyo is cooler than elsewhere
questions.explanation: The first sentence makes the general claim about Japan. 「とくに」, 'especially', introduces a specific example, Tokyo at night, which supports it.

questions.stem: Read the review: 「このラーメン屋は、駅から歩いて五分です。ねだんは少し高いですが、スープがとてもおいしいです。いつも人が多いので、早めに行ったほうがいいですよ。」 What advice does the reviewer give?
options: Take a taxi, because it is far from the station
Order the soup, because it is cheap
Go early, because it is always busy
Book ahead, because it is very small
questions.explanation: 「〜たほうがいいですよ」 gives advice, and 「いつも人が多いので」 gives the reason. The shop is five minutes' walk from the station, and the price is 「少し高い」, a little expensive.

questions.stem: Read the review: 「このえいがは話がおもしろくて、さいごまであきませんでした。でも、二時間半は少し長すぎると思います。」 What is the reviewer's view?
options: It was too short to tell its story well
The story was dull, but it was the right length
It was interesting at first but boring at the end
The story held her interest, but it was too long
questions.explanation: 「さいごまであきませんでした」 is 'I didn't get bored right to the end', and 「長すぎる」, stem + 「すぎる」, is 'too long'. 「でも」 marks the turn from praise to criticism.

questions.stem: Read: 「兄は、来年から東京の大学にかようので、今アパートをさがしています。」 Why is the brother looking for an apartment?
options: He has just started work at a company in Tokyo
He wants to leave home now to live with friends
He is studying in Tokyo and wants a cheaper place
He will attend university in Tokyo from next year
questions.explanation: 「来年から…かようので」 is 'because he will attend from next year', and 「さがしています」 is 'is searching'. Nothing mentions work, friends or cost.

questions.stem: Read: 「またバスがおくれた。これで今週三回目だ。」 How does the writer feel?
options: Relieved
Excited
Grateful
Annoyed
questions.explanation: 「また」, 'again', and 「これで今週三回目だ」, 'that's the third time this week', both show frustration. The plain forms suit a diary or a post to friends.

questions.stem: Read the advertisement: 「夏休みのアルバイトをぼしゅうしています。高校生もだいじょうぶです。時間は午前十時から午後四時までです。」 What is being advertised?
options: A summer course for high school students
Full-time jobs for university graduates
Volunteer work in the summer holidays
Holiday work open to high school students
questions.explanation: 「ぼしゅう」 is recruiting, and 「アルバイト」 is paid part-time work. 「高校生もだいじょうぶ」 tells high school students they may apply too.

questions.stem: Read the advertisement: 「日本語を楽しく勉強しませんか。はじめての人もだいかんげいです。今月中にもうしこむと、一か月分のじゅぎょうりょうがむりょうになります。」 What is the special offer?
options: Half-price lessons for the first month
Free lessons for anyone joining next month
One free month for joining this month
A free textbook for every beginner
questions.explanation: 「今月中にもうしこむと」 is 'if you apply this month', and 「一か月分のじゅぎょうりょうがむりょう」 is 'one month's fees become free'. 「だいかんげい」 welcomes beginners but offers them nothing extra.

questions.stem: Why do advertisements often use 「〜しませんか」, as in 「日本語を勉強しませんか」?
options: It tells the reader firmly what they must do
It describes something that already happened
It shows the writer is not sure of the facts
It invites the reader in a polite, friendly way
questions.explanation: 「〜ませんか」, 'won't you…?', is a polite invitation, so it draws readers in without pressure. An order would use 「〜なさい」 or 「〜なければなりません」.

questions.stem: Read the advertisement: 「このくつはかるくて歩きやすいので、旅行にぴったりです。」 Why is the shoe recommended for travel?
options: It folds up small to pack in a bag
It is light and easy to walk in
It is cheap and comes in many colours
It is warm and keeps out the rain
questions.explanation: 「かるくて」 is 'light, and', and verb stem + 「やすい」 is 'easy to', so 「歩きやすい」 is easy to walk in. 「ぴったり」 is 'perfect' for something.

questions.stem: Read the timetable note: 「京都行きの電車は、毎時十五分と四十五分に出ます。」 When do trains to Kyoto leave?
options: Every fifteen minutes throughout the day
Every forty-five minutes throughout the day
At quarter past every hour, in the morning only
At quarter past and quarter to every hour
questions.explanation: 「毎時」 is 'every hour', so trains leave at 15 and 45 minutes past each hour, two an hour. 「京都行き」 means 'bound for Kyoto'.

questions.stem: Read: 「バスは駅前を午前八時十分に出て、八時四十分にくうこうに着きます。」 How long is the trip to the airport?
options: Ten minutes
Fifty minutes
Thirty minutes
Forty minutes
questions.explanation: It leaves at 8.10 and arrives at 8.40, so the trip takes thirty minutes. 「〜に着きます」 is 'arrives at'.

questions.stem: Read the school trip plan: 「一日目は東京で買い物をします。二日目は電車でにっこうに行って、お寺や神社を見ます。三日目の朝、東京にもどります。」 What happens on the second day?
options: They spend the whole day shopping in Tokyo
They return to Tokyo in the morning
They go by bus to Nikkō to do some shopping there
By train to Nikkō to see temples and shrines
questions.explanation: 「二日目」 (ふつかめ) is the second day: 「電車でにっこうに行って」, by train to Nikkō, then 「お寺や神社を見ます」. Shopping is on the first day and the return on the third.

questions.stem: Read the notice 「日本語クラブは毎週水曜日、午後三時半からとしょかんであります。」 and the message 「今日は水曜日だよね。クラブ、行く？」 When and where does the club meet today?
options: It does not meet today
At 3.30 pm, in the library
At 3 pm, in the library
At 3.30 pm, at the school gate
questions.explanation: The message tells you today is Wednesday, and the notice says the club meets on Wednesdays at 「三時半」, 3.30, in the library. 「半」 is half past, so 3 pm is too early.

questions.stem: A text begins 「みなさん、こんにちは。今日は私のしゅみについて話します。」 What type of text is it?
options: A diary entry
A newspaper article
A speech to an audience
A personal letter
questions.explanation: 「みなさん」 addresses a group, and 「今日は…について話します」 announces a talk. A letter would open with the reader's name, and a diary has no audience.

questions.stem: Which feature is typical of a Japanese diary entry, 「にっき」?
options: Plain forms and the writer's own feelings
Polite forms and a greeting to the reader
A headline and quotes from experts
Numbered steps with 「〜てください」
questions.explanation: A diary is written for yourself, so plain forms such as 「楽しかった」 are usual, with the date and your feelings. Headlines belong to articles and numbered requests to instructions.

questions.stem: Which sentence suits a news report rather than a chatty blog?
options: 「ほんとうにびっくりしちゃった！」
「すごく楽しかったよ。」
「みんなも来てね。」
「市の人口は、この十年で少しへった。」
questions.explanation: A report gives facts in a neutral tone, often in plain form: the city's population fell a little over ten years. 「〜ちゃった」, 「すごく」 and 「〜てね」 are casual and personal.

questions.stem: A headline reads 「こうれいしゃと高校生、いっしょに町の花だんを作る」. What type of text does it begin?
options: A diary entry
A news article
A personal letter
A recipe
questions.explanation: Headlines in Japanese often drop particles and end with a plain verb, and they report what someone did, here elderly people and students making a flower bed. A letter would open with a greeting.

questions.stem: In an email, what does 「〜でしょうか」 do that 「〜ですか」 does not?
options: It makes the question sound more certain
It puts the question into the past tense
It makes the question casual and friendly
It makes the question softer and more polite
questions.explanation: 「でしょうか」 is a gentler way of asking, which suits a request to a teacher or a company: 「明日でもいいでしょうか」. It does not change the tense.

questions.stem: Read: 「すみません、電車がおくれたので、ちこくしました。」 What is the speaker doing?
options: Saying she will be late tomorrow
Explaining why she is late
Complaining to the train company
Asking the way to the station
questions.explanation: 「〜ので」 gives the reason, the train was late, and 「ちこくしました」 is 'I was late'. 「すみません」 makes it an apology with an explanation.

questions.stem: Which sentence states an opinion rather than a fact?
options: 「私の学校にはせいとが千人います。」
「先生は京都で生まれました。」
「日本語は一番おもしろいきょうかだと思います。」
「日本語のじゅぎょうは週に四回あります。」
questions.explanation: 「〜だと思います」 marks the writer's view, and 「一番おもしろい」 is a judgement others might not share. The other three can be checked.

questions.stem: Read: 「天気よほうによると、明日は雪がふるそうです。」 What is the writer doing?
options: Saying she is sure because it snowed today
Saying she hopes it will snow tomorrow
Passing on what the weather forecast said
Describing snow that is starting to fall
questions.explanation: 「〜によると」 names the source, and plain form + 「そうです」 is hearsay. If she could see snow about to fall, she would use the verb stem: 「雪がふりそうです」.

questions.stem: Read: 「まず、やさいを洗って、小さくきります。それから、なべに入れて、十分ぐらいゆでます。」 What type of text is this from?
options: An advertisement
A personal letter
A recipe
A diary entry
questions.explanation: 「まず」, 'first', and 「それから」, 'then', put steps in order, and the actions are cooking: washing, cutting, then boiling for 「十分ぐらい」 (じゅっぷんぐらい), about ten minutes.

questions.stem: In a letter to a host family you have not met, which sentence is out of place?
options: 「お会いできるのを楽しみにしています。」
「ねえ、元気？」
「はじめまして。」
「どうぞよろしくおねがいします。」
questions.explanation: 「ねえ、元気？」 is casual, for a close friend. People you have not met are written to politely: 「はじめまして」, 「どうぞよろしくおねがいします」 and the humble 「お会いできる」 all fit.
